llm.summary: The skill mostly does what it says (social-media analysis + AI generation) but includes several incoherent and potentially risky elements: embedded API keys in config.js, implicit reliance on system binaries (Chrome/Xvfb) not declared, and logic that executes other local skill scripts by absolute path.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name/description (marketing analysis, title/script generation) aligns with the code that queries APIs and saves analysis. However there are mismatches: manifest and SKILL.md claim no required binaries/env vars, yet the code expects a local Chrome binary, Xvfb/xdpyinfo and other system tooling. The Python integration script references and will execute another local skill's run_render.py via an absolute path in the user's home (~/.openclaw-agent2/...), which is not necessary for analysis and gives the skill the ability to run code outside its own directory.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs cloning and running node marketing_hub.js config <TikHubToken> <DeepSeekKey>, which is expected. But the runtime instructions in marketing_hub.js go beyond that: they attempt to start/inspect X displays, launch Chrome with execSync to scrape Douyin, run curl via child process to call DeepSeek, and the Python helper can call an external run_render.py if present. The script writes memory files to scripts/memory and can write workflows under agent_data; it also runs subprocesses and can execute other local scripts — so it reads/writes and executes files beyond the simple stated task.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only + shipping code) — no remote downloads or archive extraction. That reduces supply-chain risk compared with arbitrary download installers. However runtime uses execSync/exec/subprocess to run system tools and other local scripts, which is an operational risk rather than an install-time download risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The manifest declares no required env vars, and SKILL.md tells the user to provide TikHub and DeepSeek keys. But the repository already contains scripts/config.js with hard-coded TIKHUB_TOKEN and DEEPSEEK_KEY values — contradicting the 'doNotCommitToVcs' guidance and exposing credentials in the code bundle. Also, the skill uses DEEPSEEK_KEY directly in a curl child_process call, increasing the risk that a leaked key could be used or logged. No other unrelated credentials are requested, but the presence of committed secrets is a significant proportionality and confidentiality issue.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (good). The manifest allows filesystem read/write within ${SKILL_DIR}/scripts and ${WORKSPACE_ROOT}, and the code writes memory files under scripts/memory and agent_data; that's plausible for a memory/cache. But the skill also tries to run binaries (Chrome, Xvfb) and may execute other local skill code (absolute path to another skill's run_render.py). That cross-skill execution is disproportionate and increases blast radius because this skill can invoke local code outside its own package.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to implement the advertised marketing analysis and generation features, but there are several red flags you should consider before installing:

- Embedded secrets: scripts/config.js contains hard-coded TikHub and DeepSeek keys despite docs saying you should configure them and manifest listing config.js as doNotCommitToVcs. Treat those tokens as leaked — do not use them, and rotate any real tokens those values correspond to.

- Undeclared system dependencies: the Node script launches Chrome and manipulates X displays (Xvfb/xdpyinfo). The manifest claims no required binaries; in practice the skill needs a Chrome binary and Xvfb if you run browser scraping. Run only in an environment where you control available binaries (isolated VM/container).

- Cross-skill execution: the Python helper will call a run_render.py in a fixed path under ~/.openclaw-agent2/... if present. That lets this skill execute other local skill code. If you install, inspect that target script (run_render.py) or remove/disable the integration if you don't want this skill to run other skills.

- Shell usage and token exposure: the code uses child_process.exec / execSync / curl with the DeepSeek key; shell execution increases risk of accidental token leakage in logs. Prefer implementations that use in-process HTTPS clients and avoid embedding secrets in repo files.

Recommendations:
1) Do not use the committed config.js credentials; delete the file and run the provided config command to set your own keys, and then ensure config.js is properly ignored.
2) Review and, if desired, remove or sandbox scripts/cmd_vid_integration.py and any integration that references external skill paths.
3) Run the skill in an isolated environment (container or VM) without sensitive local skills or credentials available.
4) Verify whether you need browser scraping — if not, use the 'a' quick data mode or adapt the code to use only the documented APIs. If you must allow browser mode, ensure system binaries (Chrome/Xvfb) are intentionally provided and controlled.
5) If you trust the author and want to proceed, at minimum rotate any API keys that may have been exposed and audit network traffic and logs for unexpected endpoints.

If you want, I can: (A) point out every place in the code that spawns subprocesses/executes external files, (B) show how to remove embedded keys safely, or (C) produce a short checklist to sandbox this skill prior to running it.
